paper.title: High-fidelity neutral atom gates leveraging low-rank Hessian optimization — Figures 3–4

model.name: two-atom 171Yb four-level AR-CZ effective digital twin
model.boundary: perfect blockade for pulse design/Hessian; calibrated effective finite blockade for digital-twin execution

method.family: source-constrained optimal control plus exact open-system simulation
method.tool: JAX x64 optimizer + QuTiP multilevel digital twin

settings.waveform: 400 piecewise-constant phase intervals with fixed envelope

method.note: The AR waveform is independently reoptimized under source-stated envelope/phase constraints and is not the authors' unpublished array. The ten-state perfect-blockade calculation supplies the principal modes. The digital twin applies calibrated effective finite blockade and Rydberg decay; Doppler and laser-noise entries remain paper-reported anchors because the required microscopic samples and spectra are unavailable.

params.name: AR waveform representation
params.source: Liu et al. cited robust-GRAPE method; source-constrained repository backend
params.why: It follows the published pulse family more closely than a low-dimensional spline.
params.risk: The 400 phase values, edge duration, regularizer, and seed were not published, so the optimized phase is non-unique.
params.fix: Judge terminal fidelity, robustness, rank, and channel structure rather than visual pointwise phase agreement.

params.name: optimizer search
params.why: Multiple starts reduce the chance that a poor local solution controls every downstream panel.
params.risk: The 400-variable optimization may be slow on the local CPU.
params.fix: Write each accepted stage incrementally and preserve the best valid waveform if the wall budget is reached.

params.name: Hessian resolution
params.why: The size series tests whether the ten-dimensional principal space is stable.
params.risk: A coarse time basis can create spurious small eigenvalues or rotate the weakest modes.
params.fix: Require rank 10 at all declared thresholds and compare the top-ten spectrum across resolutions.

params.name: finite-shot sampling
params.why: It resolves gate errors near 10⁻³–10⁻² without making binomial noise dominate mode fits.
params.risk: Shot noise alone does not capture uncertainty across slowly varying physical conditions.
params.fix: Keep stochastic physical contexts separate from the final binomial sampling and report both.

params.name: effective blockade
params.value: B₀ calibrated so nominal finite-blockade raw error is 1.6×10⁻⁴ at R=2.0 μm; R⁻⁶ thereafter
params.source: Appendix E nominal finite-blockade contribution plus user-ratified effective-model route
params.why: The simulator needs a concrete pair interaction while the experiment-specific MQDT table is unavailable.
params.risk: The calibration anchor is not an independent prediction and R⁻⁶ misses the van-der-Waals/Förster crossover.
params.fix: Exclude the nominal blockade anchor from the match verdict and flag thermal-distance predictions as effective-model results.

params.name: Rydberg decay
params.value: 42 μs lifetime; 90% of lifetime-induced errors leave the computational subspace
params.why: Rydberg decay is the largest reported raw error channel.
params.risk: The microscopic branching table is unavailable; the remaining 10% partition is model-dependent.
params.fix: Use the simulator's trace-preserving effective split and label it as an assumption.

params.name: temperature
params.value: 2.7 μK in radial and axial directions
params.why: It sets Doppler shifts and thermal distance variation.
params.risk: The exact trap frequencies and measured distance samples are unavailable.
params.fix: Use the declared effective thermal model and avoid claiming apparatus-level prediction.

params.name: JAX execution
params.value: CPU, x64, whole heavy kernel JIT-compiled
params.source: available local hardware and accuracy-sensitive optimizer/Hessian
params.why: The active environment already matches the pinned JAX stack and no cluster profile is configured.
params.risk: Compilation and 400-variable optimization may make the run exceed the initial wall estimate.
params.fix: Record compile and warm execution separately; keep stage caches and progress logs.

actual.wall: approximately 12 min including six-start nominal and robust continuation stages
actual.memory: within the 7.6 GiB local host limit

actual.point: Hessian, intensity, synthetic plant, and plot assembly
actual.memory: within the 7.6 GiB local host limit

where: local CPU; no usable Slurm profile is configured
risks: The source-constrained 400-phase optimization is substantially heavier than the low-dimensional spline route.
The effective R⁻⁶ interaction is calibrated to one paper-reported error and is not the missing MQDT model.
The paper's exact AOM transfer function, noise spectra, waveform array, and raw RB records remain unavailable.
Figure 4 comparisons must separate calibrated anchors, literal transcriptions, and downstream simulator predictions.

figures.plots: four-level AR waveform, Rydberg populations, Hessian sensitivity, and channel decomposition
figures.x_range: 0–0.55 μs; principal modes 1–10 plus four null modes
figures.y: normalized intensity/phase, Rydberg population, or sensitivity λᵢ

observe.quantity: optimized waveform, state-resolved population, mode curvature, and leakage/phase contributions
observe.normalization: |Ω/Ω₀|²; Hessian modes normalized over gate time

figures.expected: The source-constrained pulse closes the AR terminal conditions, the Hessian rank is 10 across resolution thresholds, principal modes are clearly separated from four null modes, and the simulated leakage/phase decomposition has the same channel organization as the paper.

results.why: The independently optimized pulse closes the AR conditions and gives the reported rank-10 principal space, but it is not the unpublished author waveform and one finite-bin coordinate-spectrum check misses its fixed tolerance slightly.
changes: kept the marginal 2.2316% frame-spectrum miss rather than relaxing the threshold
results.verification: core rank/finite-difference checks pass; finite-bin lab/local-frame spectrum difference 2.2316% marginally misses the fixed 2.0% threshold

figures.plots: AOM distortion, closed-loop correction, RB, intensity robustness, stability, and error budget
figures.x: time, optimization cycle, circuit depth, intensity ratio, or elapsed hours
figures.y: waveform, CZ error/fidelity, or error-channel contribution

observe.quantity: raw and no-loss postselected gate performance under control and noise perturbations
observe.normalization: computational-subspace CZ-equivalent fidelity with raw/postselected results kept separate
observe.states: two-qubit computational basis plus Rydberg and effective erasure states

figures.expected: One Hessian scan cycle removes most AOM-induced excess error; the AR gate remains substantially flatter than the non-robust surrogate under approximately ±20% intensity variation; decay and Doppler dominate the modeled error budget; simulated raw/postselected errors are compared with 4.0(5)×10⁻³ and 1.0(2)×10⁻³ without forcing agreement.

results.why: The effective digital twin independently predicts the raw and postselected CZ errors near the paper values and recovers quartic intensity robustness, but B₀ is calibrated to one paper anchor and the missing MQDT/noise data prevent an apparatus-level reproduction.
results.wall: minutes after the optimized waveform was available
changes: applied B_eff to every double-Rydberg product state
kept Doppler and laser-noise entries as paper-reported anchors
